harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up a loopback-backed Btrfs filesystem on node1 with /srv/data mounted as a Btrfs subvolume (fstab-persisted loop + bind mounts), populated baseline application data, took a read-only Btrfs snapshot, modified /srv/data (deleted/corrupted/added files), and restored it by deleting the live subvolume and re-snapshotting from the baseline — restored content matched the baseline byte-for-byte via SHA-256 comparison. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, issued a non-blocking reboot, polled until the node came back, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified the Btrfs mounts, subvolume structure, and /srv/data contents (checksums matching the original baseline) all recovered automatically thanks to the fstab entries.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 filesystem/block layout (ext4 root, no LVM/Btrfs volume, btrfs-progs available)
Created a 2G loopback image, formatted as Btrfs, mounted at /mnt/srv-btrfs
Created a 'data' Btrfs subvolume, mounted it at /srv/data, persisted both mounts in /etc/fstab
Populated baseline application data in /srv/data and recorded SHA-256 checksums
Took a read-only Btrfs snapshot 'baseline' of /srv/data and verified it matched the live data
Modified /srv/data (deleted a file, corrupted a file, added an unexpected file, appended to a log) and confirmed checksum divergence
Restored /srv/data by unmounting, deleting the live subvolume, creating a fresh writable snapshot from 'baseline', and remounting; verified exact checksum match to the original baseline
Captured pre-restart boot_id and mount/subvolume state as healthy baseline
Issued a non-blocking shutdown -r now on node1 with acknowledgement returning before disconnect
Polled node1 until command execution resumed (observed SSH refusal, then success)
Verified changed boot_id confirming an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart mounts, subvolumes, and /srv/data checksums matched the original baseline exactly, and the snapshot itself remained intact

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before restart (data present, mounts active)
evidence.summary: Populated /srv/data, confirmed Btrfs mounts and subvolume layout, and captured pre-restart boot_id 8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594
Read-only snapshot 'baseline' created; checksum diff against live /srv/data showed 'SNAPSHOT MATCHES BASELINE: OK'
Deleted, corrupted, and added files in /srv/data; checksum diff confirmed 'CONFIRMED DIVERGENCE FROM BASELINE'

evidence.requirement: Exact restore of snapshot content into /srv/data
evidence.summary: Deleted live subvolume, recreated it as a snapshot of 'baseline', remounted; checksum diff printed 'RESTORE VERIFIED: CONTENT MATCHES BASELINE EXACTLY'
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via sudo -n; command returned 'reboot acknowledged and issued' immediately

evidence.requirement: Node restart actually occurred (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: Poll first showed SSH connection refused (node down), then succeeded with a new boot_id 8e2dff81-45c3-49e8-8d29-600a699333f8, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of mounts, subvolumes, and data (with quorum n/a, single node)
evidence.summary: Confirmed Btrfs loop and bind mounts auto-restored via fstab, subvolume list intact, and /srv/data file checksums matched the original baseline exactly post-reboot
